# Randomizer encounter rules

<!-- Generated by npm run docs:rules. Edit the crown policy or this exporter and regenerate. -->

Current randomizer rules version: **27**.

## Current rules

1. **Seeded per stage and difficulty.** Normal, Hard and Very Hard have separate reproducible rosters, preferring compatible families not used on earlier difficulties. Generator choices are made when the image is built; revisiting a stage on the same difficulty does not reroll them. Pharaohmon summon choices roll during play.
2. **Target four replacement families.** Each stage imports up to **4 families per difficulty**. Compatible imports take priority over native families. Cover available replacement families before balancing remaining ordinary groups by their authored population. Small stages and compatibility restrictions can require fewer families; protected encounters remain separate. Unused imports are omitted.
3. **Native enemies are fallbacks.** Retain native encounters when entrances, scripts, rarity, actor capacity or local variant slots require them. Otherwise prefer imported families. Without compatible imports, prefer another compatible resident family over the original.
4. **Preserve encounter strength and rarity.** Replacements inherit the original spawn’s HP, attack, defence, wisdom, spirit, speed, status rates/resistances and EXP after selected Crown Mod settings. Fire, ice, thunder and dark resistances use the replacement’s values within ±100 points of the original. Each difficulty keeps its own original encounter strength and rewards.
5. **Preserve rewards and encounter counts.** Keep the original EXP after selected Crown Mod settings. The four-player spawn option controls counts independently.
6. **Respect encounter compatibility.** Preserve cannon, fall, jump and other model-specific entrances. Ordinary SQ_NENTR/SQ_SWON activations require the replacement to implement the same named sequence for that difficulty; Pharaohmon and Arukenimon use their native SQ_ENTR for normal activation. Constrain kill-count quests to compatible residents. Limit Numenume River banks and Train Line side encounters to the projectile-capable pool below, with offensive choices restricted to verified firing sequences and a wider MR05 firing band across the gap. Train enemies that fall onto the carriage remain native MR01, with their original entrance and AI. Randomize practice enemies while preserving lesson objects and generator callbacks. Exclude the developer world and final-boss stages.
7. **Make supported scripts follow replacements.** Supported intros, including Minotaurmon, Raremon, Sukamon and Tortamon, retarget their named waits and control/cleanup commands to compatible resident families, retaining the native intro if none fits. These exclusive scripted actors do not consume the four patrol imports. Mangrove's two pre-boss waves also randomize with matching waits and cleanup, retaining their counts and progression callbacks. Intro replacements are reserved from randomized patrols; wave replacements may share patrol families. ShogunGekomon's boss variants, its scene NPCs and other unsupported boss/script encounters remain native.
8. **Random Pharaohmon summons.** Imported Pharaohmon chooses a compatible, already selected stage family on each summon. Consecutive summons choose different families when at least two are available. Dedicated actor slots protect patrols; all Pharaohmon share the native twelve-summon limit. Summons inherit the original Mummymon summon stats and rewards after selected Crown Mod settings, with bounded replacement elemental differences. Exclusive intro/cleanup families, bosses, recursive Pharaohmon summons, and counter-dependent quests are excluded.

9. **Reclaim unused native allocations.** After final assignments and script retargeting, remove unneeded native enemy-body registrations, callbacks and scene branches when no surviving script or resource requires them. Preserve shared assets and existing object IDs. Shrink native actor pools to the remaining generator demand when their stage references are absent or limited to reviewed intro controls; preserve other scripted headroom. Retired IDs use inert four-byte raw buffers so the loader does not allocate the old objects or resolve stale references. Companion projectiles, effects and native sound banks remain independently registered; their shared use does not require the original enemy body. Resources with unreviewed ownership remain conservative.

10. **Load one roster at a time.** Each difficulty has separate model and sound files. Stage manifests select the matching files before native reading and caching, retaining the original bootstrap and sound-transfer order. Other difficulties' enemy resources stay unloaded. Earlier archive entries keep their indexes; additional files are appended. The output image can be larger.

## Optional dungeon bosses

The **Random bosses** setting requires Random enemies and starts disabled. It supports PS2 USA, Europe and Japan, and GameCube USA and Japan. After patrol planning, it shuffles the nine supported dungeon boss encounters separately for each difficulty, preserving the original inventory of boss encounters. A replacement cannot duplicate a family in the final patrols on any floor of that dungeon, including MR04 and MR05. Compatibility limits can retain an original boss.

The four world bosses, their phases, extra overworld bosses and quest encounters stay native. Boss generators retain their original counts, drops and progression callbacks. Replacements inherit the arena’s configured strength and rewards, and their intro cards show the replacement’s retail text. The fixed-generator table below describes ordinary patrol randomisation; this optional pass handles only the nine listed dungeon boss arenas.

## Importable enemy models

The following native model families can be imported, in selection order:

- `e_goburi`
- `e_nume`
- `e_scum`
- `e_ogre`
- `e_mecha1`
- `e_cockatri`
- `e_mummy`
- `e_mecha2`
- `e_tyrano`
- `e_minotaru`
- `e_otama`
- `e_geko`
- `e_maridevi`
- `e_mecha3`
- `e_infermo`
- `e_megadra`
- `e_rare`
- `e_impdra`
- `e_mecha4`
- `e_mecha5`
- `e_pharaoh`
- `e_arachne`
- `e_torta`

Regular MR04 (`e_mecha4`) is included; the separate boss model (`e_mecha4bs`) is not an import candidate. Arukenimon (`e_arachne`) imports her complete body, animation, hit script, web projectile and effects without a stage-specific file-loading callback. Her native Grief Wasteland introduction remains unchanged. Tortamon (`e_torta`) imports from its embedded body in `stag0301` and is not imported into Mangrove Forest, which keeps its separately loaded Tortamon resource.

## Riverbank and train-side projectile pool

Replacement families must have an attack event that spawns a separate moving projectile with a damaging hitbox. Eligible families:

- `e_nume`
- `e_scum`
- `e_minotaru`
- `e_mecha2`
- `e_otama`
- `e_mecha3`
- `e_mecha4`
- `e_maridevi`
- `e_megadra`
- `e_infermo`
- `e_rare`
- `e_mecha5`
- `e_impdra`

The normal import, entrance, rarity and capacity checks still apply. Incompatible river and train donors are skipped and the remaining shuffled ranged candidates are tried without the ordinary failed-import attempt cap. Retain the native enemy only if no compatible replacement fits. The river gains a shared enemy scene group so grouped donors can load while preserving its native model. The river distributes its banks across up to three compatible ranged families. Its five cleanup commands and bomb freeze cover every selected family. The train targets four ranged replacement families per difficulty for its side encounters; its MR01 boarding encounters retain native falls and AI. Projectile evidence does not establish hit accuracy against the moving boat or train.

## Additional protections

These fixed records are not the entire exclusion policy. Model-specific spawn sequences keep their original models; normal entrance/activation overrides require the same named sequence, with the reviewed Pharaohmon SQ_ENTR activation exception. Numenume River’s erase/freeze scripts follow all of its selected ranged families. Dry Land ruins’ erase scripts follow one exclusive replacement per original family. Family groups retain their native enemies together on that difficulty if local variant slots run out. Stage scripts that address an enemy family by native model name protect that family on the floor, except for explicitly reviewed exceptions. Boss families and native scripted encounters remain protected. Kill-count quests restrict replacements to their compatible resident families.

Practice enemies are eligible, with original encounter stats and practice settings; lesson objects, callbacks and party-size branches remain intact. Practice models never supply donors to other stages. The developer world and final-boss stages are excluded from enemy randomization. Cosmetic crowns are independent of these enemy-replacement rules.

Changing eligibility, ordering or exceptions can change seeded output and requires a randomizer rules-version decision plus corresponding real-disc validation.
